context: Responsive scatter plot of employee salary vs. years of experience shown at 6 container sizes (640px→80px) using CSS container queries and ResizeObserver, with linked cross-panel hover highlighting
first_impression: A technically polished multi-panel scatter that degrades gracefully to sparkline and KPI modes, with honest encoding throughout.
what_works: Both axes use d3.extent() for data-driven domains with .nice(); dot identity uses d => d.id key function for correct joins; trend line is computed via proper least-squares regression with R² displayed; no zero-baseline violation since scatter plots are exempt.
what_doesnt: Y-axis starts at ~$55k (extent-based), so removing the minimum-salary point would shift the axis and cause subset-relation instability — a minor robustness gap; dot radius is hardcoded per breakpoint rather than derived from a scale, making the sparkline-to-full size jump arbitrary rather than proportional.
